=== THE PROBLEM ===

`python3 ringer.py models` prints a scoreboard read by an orchestrator AT DECISION TIME. It currently displays rows for lanes that have been DELETED from the fleet. The worst example: `qwen3.8-max-preview` displays as tier 'proven', 15 tasks, 100% pass -- an attractive, high-scoring row for a lane that cannot be dispatched to at all. That is a board lying to a decision-maker.

Retired harnesses/engines, all gone from ~/.config/ringer/config.toml: `qwencode`, `qwenclaude`, `kimiqwen`, `qwen`, `kimiclaude`. The live engines are exactly: `codex`, `claude`, `kimi`, `mock`.

In the live log (~/.ringer/runs.jsonl, 413 rows) roughly 111 rows reference qwen and 48 reference kimiclaude.

=== WHAT TO CHANGE ===

Make `ringer.py models` hide rows belonging to retired harnesses, and say so.

- DO NOT delete, rewrite or filter the eval log itself. The rows are history and stay on disk untouched. This is a DISPLAY change only.
- Suppress rows whose harness/engine is one of the retired names above, from the text scoreboard.
- Print exactly one summary line when anything was hidden, containing the word `retired` and the number of suppressed rows, e.g. `  (37 rows from retired lanes hidden: qwencode, kimiclaude)`. Never hide silently -- a board that quietly drops data is the same defect in a different direction.
- If nothing was hidden, print no such line.
- Keep the change small and local to the rendering path. Do not restructure the scoreboard, do not add a CLI flag, do not add dependencies.

=== HOW TO VERIFY ===

Run from the repo root:

    python3 ringer.py models

It must (a) contain no `qwen` and no `kimiclaude` anywhere, (b) still show live models such as GPT-5.6 Sol and Kimi K3, (c) print the one retired-rows line. Then confirm you destroyed nothing:

    grep -c qwen ~/.ringer/runs.jsonl

must still report the same count as before your change (~111).

Also run the focused suite -- do NOT run the whole suite, it has a known unrelated pre-existing failure in tests/test_contributors.py:

    python3 -m unittest tests.test_effort_attribution_acceptance tests.test_catalog -q

=== OUTPUT CONTRACT ===

Edit ringer.py, then write ./notes.md in the scratch dir: what you changed, where, the exact commands you ran and their output, and anything you were unsure about.

You are adding one safety guard to a real repository. Your working directory is a scratch dir -- use it only for ./notes.md. The repo you may edit is /Users/austinli/fleet/swarm.

OWNERSHIP BOUNDARY: you own exactly ONE file: /Users/austinli/fleet/swarm/overlay/deploy.py. Another worker is editing ringer.py at the same time -- do not touch it, do not revert it, do not be alarmed by it. Do not edit anything under tests/. Do not touch .git, do not commit, do not push.

=== WHY ===

overlay/deploy.py reproduces this operator's setup on another machine. It OVERWRITES ~/.claude/rules/model-routing.md and other files, backing each up first.

On 2026-07-27 that overwrite ran from a laptop whose evidence file was three days stale. It silently reverted a measured routing decision made on the destination machine. Backups existed, but nobody looks at backups they do not know they need -- detection was pure luck. The fix is not merge machinery (two machines, one operator). It is a loud conflict instead of a silent clobber.

=== WHAT TO ADD ===

Both files carry dated entry headings of the form `## 2026-07-25 — title`. Add TWO module-level functions to overlay/deploy.py with EXACTLY these names and signatures:

    def newest_datestamp(text: str) -> str | None
        Return the latest YYYY-MM-DD that appears as a MARKDOWN HEADING stamp,
        i.e. on a line beginning with '##' followed by the date. Return None if
        there is none. A date sitting in ordinary prose is NOT an entry stamp and
        must be ignored. Dates are ISO so string comparison is sufficient.

    def staleness_conflict(src_text: str, dst_text: str) -> str | None
        Return None when it is safe to overwrite. Return a human-readable
        multi-line message when the DESTINATION is NEWER than the source --
        i.e. we are about to clobber work the incoming file has never seen. The
        message must contain BOTH date strings so the operator can see the gap.
        Safe cases (return None): source newer, dates equal, destination empty
        (fresh install), destination has no datestamp at all.

Then WIRE IT IN: before deploy.py overwrites ~/.claude/rules/model-routing.md, compare the incoming overlay source against what is already on disk. On conflict, print the message and ABORT the deploy with a non-zero exit -- do not write, do not half-write other files. Under `--check` report the conflict the same way rather than pretending the deploy would succeed.

Keep it small -- roughly 15-25 lines plus the wiring. Stdlib only, no dependencies. Match the file's existing style (it is plain, typed, argparse-based).

=== HOW TO VERIFY ===

Run from the repo root:

    python3 -m unittest tests.test_deploy_staleness_acceptance -q
    python3 overlay/test_deploy.py
    python3 overlay/deploy.py --check

The first is the grading check -- read tests/test_deploy_staleness_acceptance.py for the exact contract, but DO NOT edit it. The third must still succeed on this machine (its rules file and the overlay source currently carry the same newest stamp, so there is no conflict here).

=== OUTPUT CONTRACT ===

Edit overlay/deploy.py, then write ./notes.md in the scratch dir: what you added, where you wired the check in, the exact commands you ran and their output, and anything you were unsure about.
